class.name: TimeOfDay
class.brief_description: Moves a sun and a moon across the sky as the hours pass, and dims the sky at night.
class.description: Add a [TimeOfDay] with two [DirectionalLight3D] children: the first is the sun and the second the moon (or set [member sun] and [member moon]). As [member time] passes, it points them from where they are in the sky, sets their energy and colour (warm and low at dawn and dusk, white at noon, a dim blue moon at night) and turns off whichever is below the horizon. In a running game it also dims the sky and ambient light of the world's [Environment] at night, down to [member night_sky_energy] of their own values. The sun rises in the node's +X direction and is due +Z at noon, so turn the node to set where north is. In the editor, changing [member time] shows that hour, but the clock only runs in a game.

method.name: get_daylight
method.description: How much daylight there is: [code]1.0[/code] by day, [code]0.0[/code] at night, and in between round sunrise and sunset.

method.name: get_sun_direction
method.description: The direction towards the sun, in global space.

method.name: is_day
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the sun is above the horizon.

members.member: How many real seconds a day takes. [code]0[/code] stops the clock.
How far north (or south, below [code]0[/code]) the place is, in degrees: the further from the equator, the lower the sun stays.
The light for the moon. When it's empty, the first [DirectionalLight3D] child that isn't the sun is used.
The moon's energy when it's high in the sky.
How bright the sky and ambient light are at night, as a part of their own energies.
The light for the sun. When it's empty, the first [DirectionalLight3D] child is used.
The sun's energy when it's high in the sky.
The time of day in hours, from [code]0.0[/code] (midnight) to [code]24.0[/code]: [code]13.5[/code] is half past one in the afternoon.

signal.name: hour_changed
signal.description: Emitted as each hour begins, with the hour from [code]0[/code] to [code]23[/code]: for every hour in turn, even when a frame spans several.
